Losing our first big customer was the best thing that ever happened to Ledgerline.

Let me explain.

5 months in, they walked away. It stung. A lot.

But failure isn't the opposite of success. It's part of it.

The reason they left: they had heavily customized their NetSuite instance, and we only supported standard fields. We weren't meeting them where they were.

So we did what good teams do. We listened. We learned. We built.

We spent 6 weeks adding support for custom fields. That changed how we think about our customers, not just our product.

Today, we serve 38 customers. 11 of them rely on custom fields.

The lesson? Your biggest setback can become your biggest breakthrough.

Lean into the hard feedback. Your customers are telling you what to build. You just have to listen.

What's a loss that shaped your company?

#Startups #SaaS #Leadership #CustomerSuccess #Growth

1,200 repositories.

When we launched Patchwork CI, we promised it would stay free for open source. People told us we were crazy. How would we make money, they asked.

Open source gave us more than users. It gave us data, feedback, and a community. Our most-requested feature, GitLab support, came straight from OSS maintainers. We shipped it on November 12.

Giving back is not charity. It is strategy.

#OpenSource #DevOps #CI #DeveloperExperience #BuildInPublic

We built an app we loved. Almost nobody used it.

When we launched Rotaship, the mobile app looked sharp. We figured restaurant staff would pick it up fast.

They didn't. Only 12% of staff opened it in the first month.

That stung, but it taught us something. We weren't solving the real problem. We were adding to it.

Restaurant teams don't want another app. They already live on WhatsApp.

So in 2025 we killed the app and moved everything into WhatsApp.

It worked. 140 outlets now use it, and the median reply time to shift messages is under 20 minutes.

If you're building for busy people, build where they already are. Don't ask them to come to you.

Sometimes the best product decision is letting go of the thing you love.

Day after day, I saw anxious pets so terrified that we had to sedate them just to examine them.

I knew there had to be a better way.

So in 2023, I took the leap and founded Doorstep Vet.

Today, our team of 4 vets does around 30 home visits a week. Every single one reminds me why we do this.

Calmer pets. Happier owners. Better medicine.

Sometimes the bravest thing you can do is follow your heart.

Mistakes don't define you. How you respond to them does.

To all the hardware founders out there: own your mistakes, fix them fast, and build systems so they never happen again.
